CID_a02080_4010g_00110_02080_1: \nHe'd been joking around, so surely he's going to be okay.:<TAP>
CID_a02080_4010g_00130_02080_1: \n\nI feel like the uncertainty will crush me under its weight.:<NONE>
CID_a02080_4010g_00200_02080_1: Finally, my husband emerges from the infirmary.:<TAP>
CID_a02080_4010g_00210_02080_1: \n\nSeeing him safe, I let out a small gasp of relief.:<TAP>
CID_a02080_4010g_00220_02080_1: \nHowever, he has no memory of the recent past...:<TAP>
CID_a02080_4010g_00300_02080_1: The memory loss is due to shock, and only temporary—:<TAP>
CID_a02080_4010g_00310_02080_1: \nbut no one can explain where the photo went.:<TAP>
CID_a02080_4010g_00320_02080_1:
My husband, as if sensing my unease, wraps me up in
another tight embrace.:<NONE>
CID_a02080_4010g_00400_02080_1: As I feel his <size=40> warmth</size>, my concerns melt away once more.:<TAP>
CID_a02080_4010g_00410_02080_1: \nSo long as you are safe, that's all that matters.:
CID_a02080_4010g_00420_02080_1: \nIt is the only thing that matters...:
CID_a02090_1010g_00100_02090_1: I inhale a lungful of battlefield air, rich with a mix of\ngunsmoke and blood.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_1010g_00110_02090_1:
Our operation was a smashing success, but while my fellow
soldiers are content going back to base and celebrating our victory,
I'm heading out on a new mission.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_1010g_00120_02090_1: \nBecause the only time I feel alive now is when I fight.:<NONE>
CID_a02090_1010g_00200_02090_1: Revenge drove me. It's all that ever drove me.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_1010g_00210_02090_1: \nBut then I ended up killing my own father.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_1010g_00220_02090_1: \nAnd on top of that, it turns out the people I called my family\nwere actually my enemies.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_1010g_00230_02090_1: \nWhat a goddamn joke, right? Anybody else laughing here?:<NONE>
CID_a02090_1010g_00300_02090_1: When I return to reality, I see piles of corpses everywhere.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_1010g_00310_02090_1: \nIt's all my doing, this carnage, but instead of rage or sorrow,\nI just feel a strange sense of calm.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_1010g_00320_02090_1: \nHonestly, killing is the only thing that brings me peace anymore.:<NONE>
CID_a02090_1010g_00400_02090_1: Suddenly, an explosion shakes the ground—a close one.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_1010g_00410_02090_1: \nThe sky turns red as flames arc up toward the heavens.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_1010g_00420_02090_1: \nAs I stare at this crimson sky, my heart begins to race.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_1010g_00430_02090_1: \nI set out in search of someone to fight, hoping to calm my jangled nerves.:<NONE>
CID_a02090_2010g_00100_02090_1: The war has turned in our favor.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_2010g_00110_02090_1: \nThe enemies we don't kill we send running into the night...:<TAP>
CID_a02090_2010g_00130_02090_1: \nI find myself picking my way across a viscera-strewn battlefield\njust in case we missed a straggler.:<NONE>
CID_a02090_2010g_00200_02090_1: After a bit, I sense someone hiding behind a collapsed house.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_2010g_00220_02090_1: \nI raise my sword and leap out of hiding, prepared to strike down my terrible foe.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_2010g_00230_02090_1: \nBut there, crouching on the ground, is a little girl.:<NONE>
CID_a02090_2010g_00310_02090_1: We're under orders to protect civilians, which means I gotta \ndrag this kid around with me until I find a place to dump her off. :
CID_a02090_2010g_00330_02090_1: \nI extend a bloody hand and grab the girl by the arm.:<NONE>
CID_a02090_2010g_00410_02090_1: \nI give her a good yank and start walking.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_2010g_00420_02090_1: \nShe responds by pinwheeling her other arm and toppling\nface-down into the mud.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_2010g_00430_02090_1: \n\nThat's when I realize the kid is blind.:<NONE>
CID_a02090_3010g_00100_02090_1: The girl, still sitting on the ground, grabs my hand and says,:<TAP>
CID_a02090_3010g_00110_02090_1: \n\n"Oh no, mister! You're bleeding. Are you okay?":<TAP>
CID_a02090_3010g_00120_02090_1: \n\nThe question hits me wrong, and I smack her hand away.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_3010g_00130_02090_1: \nAfter that, we wait in a long, uncomfortable silence.:<NONE>
CID_a02090_3010g_00200_02090_1: "It's not my blood," I say finally,:<TAP>
CID_a02090_3010g_00210_02090_1: \n\nas much to break the silence as anything else.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_3010g_00220_02090_1:
I wipe my hand on my pants to clear off as much gore as I can, 
then help the kid up.:<NONE>
CID_a02090_3010g_00320_02090_1: \nThe only thing mine are good for any more is murder;\nit's hard to believe her hands and mine are the same thing.:<NONE>
CID_a02090_3010g_00400_02090_1: With no other choice, I throw her across my back and start\nworking my way back to base.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_3010g_00410_02090_1: \nI can feel the kid's warmth against me.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_3010g_00420_02090_1: \nAnd there, in the strange silence you always get on a\nbattlefield after a fight...:<TAP>
CID_a02090_3010g_00430_02090_1: \nThe only thing I can hear is the beating of my own heart.:<NONE>
CID_a02090_4010g_00100_02090_1: Eventually, we make it to a field hospital.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_4010g_00110_02090_1: \nIt's a nice place, actually, with sunlight coming through the\nwindows and wind rustling the trees.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_4010g_00120_02090_1: \nThe kid seems okay with it, at least.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_4010g_00130_02090_1: \nShe lies on a bed, her gaze trained on the window to her side.:<NONE>
CID_a02090_4010g_00210_02090_1: \n"What were you doing on the ground back there?":<TAP>
CID_a02090_4010g_00220_02090_1: \nShe pauses for a second, then speaks.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_4010g_00230_02090_1: \nShe tells me how she'd been neglected by her parents her whole life\nbefore they finally abandoned her once the war came home.:<NONE>
CID_a02090_4010g_00300_02090_1: When her story is done, she turns her head in my direction\nand asks::<TAP>
CID_a02090_4010g_00310_02090_1: \n\n"What color is the sky right now, mister?":<TAP>
CID_a02090_4010g_00320_02090_1: \n\nI take a look out the window.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_4010g_00340_02090_1: \nShe closes her eyes—I have no idea why—and begins to try and\nimagine what blue might look like.:
CID_a02090_4010g_00400_02090_1: I don't know why I feel uneasy here, but I do.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_4010g_00410_02090_1: \nSomething about being near this kid puts me on edge.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_4010g_00420_02090_1: \nMy heart is racing again—but in a different way\nthan the discomfort I've felt for my entire life.:<TAP>
CID_a02090_4010g_00430_02090_1: \nAnd as I try to identify what this strange feeling is,\nI picture the <size=40>color of the sky</size> in the girl's imagination.:<NONE>
CID_a02100_1010g_00110_02100_1:
I sit in the briefing room, continuing to turn the problem
over and over in my mind.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_1010g_00120_02100_1:
I've been up all night thinking about it
and am now beyond exhausted.:<NONE>
CID_a02100_1010g_00200_02100_1: See, I have to write a telegram to my family back home,:<TAP>
CID_a02100_1010g_00210_02100_1: \nbut I can't think of a single thing to say.:<NONE>
CID_a02100_1010g_00300_02100_1:
My squad came back victorious from battle a few days ago,
at which point everyone sat down and wrote their parents
just like always.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_1010g_00310_02100_1: \n\nI joined the army eight years ago...:<TAP>
CID_a02100_1010g_00320_02100_1: \nAnd I haven't contacted my family a single time.:<NONE>
CID_a02100_1010g_00400_02100_1: It would be strange to send them something now. Crazy.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_1010g_00410_02100_1:
And every time I think back on my time with them,
I come up with more excuses not to do it.:<NONE>
CID_a02100_2010g_00100_02100_1: My fellow soldiers are loud and boisterous, like always.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_2010g_00110_02100_1: \nI begin to wonder what kinds of messages they send.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_2010g_00120_02100_1: \nI sit still and listen in, hoping it will give me a better idea\nof what to write.:<NONE>
CID_a02100_2010g_00200_02100_1: One man says he sent his parents a telegram about being\npromoted to captain.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_2010g_00210_02100_1:
It's not true—he made it up—but his parents love hearing 
stories about how successful he is, so he figures it's okay 
to stretch the truth a little.:<NONE>
CID_a02100_2010g_00300_02100_1: Another man's telegrams always focus on memories he \nand his parents made together.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_2010g_00310_02100_1:
Today's letter is all about how they used to play ball with
each other; he claims it will distract them from how lonely
they are now that he's gone.:<NONE>
CID_a02100_2010g_00400_02100_1:
Everyone speaks so cheerfully about the thought they put into
telegrams home.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_2010g_00410_02100_1: \nAnd though they are my comrades—and my friends—:<TAP>
CID_a02100_2010g_00420_02100_1: \n\nI can't help but feel the gulf between our lives.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_2010g_00430_02100_1: \nThe worlds we grew up in were too different.:<NONE>
CID_a02100_3010g_00100_02100_1: Here's the thing: Ours is a country that values military might\nabove all else, but my parents?:<TAP>
CID_a02100_3010g_00120_02100_1: \nNeedless to say, their beliefs earned me more than my share\nof dirty looks and unkind whispers when I was a kid.:<NONE>
CID_a02100_3010g_00200_02100_1: One day, the army shot and killed my father. \nWhat a joke, right?:<TAP>
CID_a02100_3010g_00210_02100_1: \nHe's spent his entire life preaching peace, then died without\naccomplishing a single damn thing.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_3010g_00220_02100_1: I took a lesson from that: Give your life some meaning. Make it matter.:
CID_a02100_3010g_00300_02100_1: Later, I decided to join the army and climb the ranks—but when\nI told Mom about my plan, she said I was insane.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_3010g_00310_02100_1: \nThe moment she spoke those words, \nI knew I had to get out of that house.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_3010g_00320_02100_1: \nSo I slammed the door and stormed off, then spent years trying\nand failing to forget the empty look in her eyes as I departed.:<NONE>
CID_a02100_3010g_00400_02100_1: In an ironic twist, I never did climb the ladder the way I\nswore I would.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_3010g_00410_02100_1:
But today, after eight years spent trying to bury every last
memory of my family, I finally figure out the telegram I want
to send::<TAP>
CID_a02100_4010g_00100_02100_1: I'm nervous after I send the telegram. What if she doesn't respond?:<TAP>
CID_a02100_4010g_00110_02100_1: \nHell, what if she disowns me? I couldn't blame her for that.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_4010g_00120_02100_1: But before I can think too hard about it, I get her response: Honey, I'm just so glad you're alive.:
CID_a02100_4010g_00200_02100_1: Why was my father an anti-war activist, anyway?:<TAP>
CID_a02100_4010g_00210_02100_1: \nWhy did my joining the army weigh so heavily on my mother?:<TAP>
CID_a02100_4010g_00220_02100_1:
I don't have a clue, because I've spent my whole life
actively avoiding a search for those answers.:<NONE>
CID_a02100_4010g_00300_02100_1: The mistakes I made in the past will never go away.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_4010g_00310_02100_1:
But as I think of my military companions and their families,
another thought comes to me::<NONE>
CID_a02100_4010g_00400_02100_1: I risked my life for these people. Gave everything for them.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_4010g_00410_02100_1: \n\nAnd I'm more proud of that fact than anything else.:<TAP>
CID_a02100_4010g_00420_02100_1: \nBut while I salute them, I doubt it will convey these\n<size=40>feelings</size> that well up within me.:<NONE>
CID_a02110_1010g_00100_02110_1: When I open my eyes, a strange sensation lingers in my mind.:<style="Dash>
CID_a02110_1010g_00200_02110_1: In my dream, I was flying before I fell from the sky.:<TAP>
CID_a02110_1010g_00210_02110_1: \nIt is the same dream I always have.:<NONE>
CID_a02110_1010g_00300_02110_1: I hear dreams are what humans experience \nwhile undergoing memory reorganization.:<TAP>
CID_a02110_1010g_00310_02110_1: \nBut if this is true, why do I have this dream?\nI have never flown; I have no memories of it.:
CID_a02110_1010g_00400_02110_1: Maybe I only wish I could fly.:
CID_a02110_1010g_00420_02110_1: \n\nOr maybe it's an influence from my older sister—the original.:<NONE>
CID_a02110_2010g_00100_02110_1: I didn't dream today—or maybe I did and I just don't remember.:<TAP>
CID_a02110_2010g_00120_02110_1: \nI hear that's possible as well, though you'd think I would know,\nconsidering that I'm dealing with my own body.:<NONE>
CID_a02110_2010g_00200_02110_1: We constructs are not supposed to need sleep.:<TAP>
CID_a02110_2010g_00210_02110_1:
Not to say that we could perpetually act autonomously—
just that it was planned that we'd undergo regular
maintenance instead.:<NONE>
CID_a02110_2010g_00300_02110_1: But I'm different. I'm the only one who sleeps. Who dreams.:<TAP>
CID_a02110_2010g_00320_02110_1: \nI dream of memories that do not belong to me,\nmemories that intermingle with my own feelings.:<NONE>
CID_a02110_2010g_00400_02110_1: I do not know why I am the only one to do so.:<TAP>
CID_a02110_2010g_00410_02110_1: \nBut my dreams are indispensable to me.:<TAP>
CID_a02110_3010g_00100_02110_1: I dreamed again today—or rather, I remember my dream.:<TAP>
CID_a02110_3010g_00111_02110_1: \nI dreamed I met someone living in a small forest hut.:<NONE>
CID_a02110_3010g_00200_02110_1: I concentrate on the sensations I felt while sleeping,\nand I am overcome by the sense I am unable to breathe.:<TAP>
CID_a02110_3010g_00210_02110_1: \n\nThis memory most certainly belonged to my elder sister.:<NONE>
CID_a02110_3010g_00300_02110_1: I cannot easily reach my elder sister's memories;\nit is like trying to navigate a path covered in fog.:<TAP>
CID_a02110_3010g_00310_02110_1: \nPerhaps this is an effect of her losing control.:<NONE>
CID_a02110_3010g_00400_02110_1: But my dreams are so far removed from reality.:<TAP>
CID_a02110_3010g_00410_02110_1: \n\nAfter all, I have never seen a human before.:<NONE>
CID_a02110_4010g_00100_02110_1: When I finally exit the facility and make my way outside,\nI find more lush nature—and ruined cities—\nthan in my memories.:<TAP>
CID_a02110_4010g_00110_02110_1: \n\nAnd I also find hordes of machines.:<NONE>
CID_a02110_4010g_00200_02110_1: But I see no humans anywhere. Not a single one.:<TAP>
CID_a02110_4010g_00210_02110_1: \nThe sight is so different from my elder sister's\nmemories when she used to live on the surface.:<NONE>
CID_a02110_4010g_00300_02110_1: How long have I been asleep? How long did I dream?:<TAP>
CID_a02110_4010g_00310_02110_1: \nThere is no way for me to know the answer.:<NONE>
CID_a02110_4010g_00400_02110_1: Will I ever reach the place from my sister's memory?:<TAP>
CID_a02110_4010g_00410_02110_1: \n\nThe only clues I have come to me as I <size=40>dream</size>.:<NONE>
CID_b01060_1010g_00100_01060_1: We were a perfectly average family leading a perfectly average life.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_1010g_00200_01060_1: \n\nI used to love Sundays when I was little.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_1010g_00300_01060_1: \nIt was the one day of the week I got to spend with Mom, Dad, and my little brother.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_1010g_00500_01060_1: And cooking is such an adventure for a little kid.:
CID_b01060_1010g_00600_01060_1: \n\nI'd try to copy the cooking video playing on the tablet, but every time I went to crack an egg, things got...interesting.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_1010g_00700_01060_1: \n\nI'd go through an entire carton trying to get it right, and Dad would laugh each time I didn't.:<PAGE>
CID_b01060_1010g_00800_01060_1: One day, I finally got my egg in the pan with a minimal amount of shell. I whispered the magic word for my secret flipping technique and...:
CID_b01060_1010g_01000_01060_1: \nMy brother poked the ticklish spot on my side, causing the egg to smear all over the pan.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_1010g_01100_01060_1: \n\nHe was always such a little jerk...:<PAGE>
CID_b01060_1010g_01200_01060_1: Anyway, I draped the remains of the egg over some golden rice and called it good.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_1010g_01300_01060_1: \n\nThen I drew a smiling sun on it with ketchup and gave it to Dad.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_1010g_01400_01060_1: \n\n"This looks just like you," he said. And just like a sun, I beamed.:<PAGE>
CID_b01060_2010g_00100_01060_1: It was the first parents' visiting day of my elementary school life.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_2010g_00200_01060_1: \n\nThe unusual prospect of a family visit set the class abuzz.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_2010g_00300_01060_1: \nEven our teacher—who was terrifying when angry—seemed nervous.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_2010g_00400_01060_1: \n\nDad even took off work so he could come.:<PAGE>
CID_b01060_2010g_00500_01060_1: Our first class of the day was social studies, followed by science and math.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_2010g_00600_01060_1: \n\nWhenever the teacher asked who knew an answer, I waved my hand over my head like a crazy person and screamed, "Me, me, me!":<TAP>
CID_b01060_2010g_00700_01060_1: \n\nDad watched as I breezily wrote the answer down on the blackboard.:<PAGE>
CID_b01060_2010g_00800_01060_1: In our final class, the students had to give a presentation about the origins of our names.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_2010g_00900_01060_1: \n\nEveryone seemed embarrassed by their parents' reasons for choosing names.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_2010g_01000_01060_1: \n\nBut I was ready. The day before, Dad said they named me Hina because it means "sunshine.":<TAP>
CID_b01060_2010g_01100_01060_1: \n\nWe wanted you to smile as brightly as the sun, he'd said.:
CID_b01060_2010g_01200_01060_1: When I was finished, my teacher told me my name suited me perfectly.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_2010g_01300_01060_1: \n"You do have a very bright smile! It always cheers me up.":
CID_b01060_2010g_01400_01060_1: \n\nMy friends all agreed, and I felt like I was going to explode with pride.:<PAGE>
CID_b01060_3010g_00100_01060_1: When I got to high school, our family underwent a seismic shift.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_3010g_00300_01060_1: \n\nWe used to cook together on the weekend. Go on trips together. Now everything was different.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_3010g_00400_01060_1: \nI thought happy families like ours only got ripped apart in TV shows.:<PAGE>
CID_b01060_3010g_00500_01060_1: I ended up living with Dad.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_3010g_00600_01060_1: \n\nHe was mentally and emotionally broken, and no longer smiled like he used to.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_3010g_00700_01060_1: \n\nHe'd just lay down and stare into space. Even breathing seemed to cause him pain.:<PAGE>
CID_b01060_3010g_00800_01060_1: The people around me all worried about him.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_3010g_01000_01060_1: \nThey constantly asked if I was doing okay, and seemed to be searching for a way to connect with me.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_3010g_01100_01060_1: \n\nBut I just smiled and said everything was fine.:<PAGE>
CID_b01060_3010g_01200_01060_1: Even if it wasn't. Even if I was miserable.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_3010g_01300_01060_1: \n\nBecause as long as I kept smiling...:<TAP>
CID_b01060_3010g_01400_01060_1: \n\nI thought there was a chance Dad would go back to his old self.:<PAGE>
CID_b01060_4010g_00100_01060_1: The days following the divorce turned into weeks. Months.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_4010g_00200_01060_1: \n\nI tried everything I could think of to get our lives back, all while going to school.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_4010g_00300_01060_1: \n\nI just wanted a life like everyone else.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_4010g_00400_01060_1: \nBut if Dad and I ever wanted to get there, I was going to have to put in some serious work.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_4010g_00500_01060_1: \nAnd I had no idea just how far we'd actually fallen.:<PAGE>
CID_b01060_4010g_00600_01060_1: One day, I was having a mindless chat with a friend on the phone.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_4010g_00700_01060_1: \nWe were gossiping about random things at school.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_4010g_00800_01060_1: \n\nNear the end of the call, she got serious and asked if everything was okay at home.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_4010g_00900_01060_1: \n\n"Everything's fine!" I replied in a chipper voice.:<PAGE>
CID_b01060_4010g_01200_01060_1: \n\nI could see my reflection in its surface, my face strained under the weight of a false smile.:<PAGE>
CID_b01060_4010g_01300_01060_1: And in that moment, I understood everything.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_4010g_01400_01060_1: \n\nMy parents chose my name because they wanted me to smile as brightly as the sun.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_4010g_01500_01060_1: \n\nBut it quickly became a curse that bound me.:<TAP>
CID_b01060_4010g_01600_01060_1: \nBecause no matter how hard or painful my life...:<TAP>
CID_b01060_4010g_01700_01060_1: \n\nEveryone expected me to have a brilliant, beaming smile on my face.:<PAGE>
CID_b01070_1010g_00100_01070_1: It happened when I started elementary school.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_1010g_00200_01070_1: \nI used to come home crying every day.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_1010g_00300_01070_1: \n\nI was extremely shy, and my classmates saw that weakness and took to bullying me.:<PAGE>
CID_b01070_1010g_00400_01070_1: I'd try to wipe the tears away and put on a brave face, but Mom always knew.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_1010g_00500_01070_1: \n\nShe'd ask if something happened, and I would just nod.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_1010g_00600_01070_1: \n\nShe never said anything else; she'd just sit there and quietly stroke my hair.:<PAGE>
CID_b01070_1010g_00700_01070_1: I remember moonlight pouring in through a window.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_1010g_00800_01070_1: \nI used to lie in her bed while she sang me a lullaby.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_1010g_00900_01070_1: \n\nI don't remember the words exactly, but it went something like this::<TAP>
CID_b01070_1010g_01000_01070_1: \n\n"Though the moon stands alone in the night sky, its gentle light shows the way for everyone else.":<PAGE>
CID_b01070_1010g_01100_01070_1: Part of my name means "moon"—Mom apparently named me after the lullaby.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_1010g_01200_01070_1: \n\nShe wanted me to be the kind of person who helped others. Even if no one sought me out specifically. Even if I didn't fit in.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_1010g_01300_01070_1: \n\nThe moment she told me this, I swore to become the moon.:<PAGE>
CID_b01070_2010g_00100_01070_1: I was shy as ever when I started middle school.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_2010g_00200_01070_1: \n\nEveryone else could just strike up conversations with perfect strangers, and they all had tons of new friends within the first week.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_2010g_00300_01070_1: \nI couldn't begin to fathom how their brains worked.:<PAGE>
CID_b01070_2010g_00400_01070_1: But I was used to being alone.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_2010g_00500_01070_1: \n\nAround that time, I saw a boy in glasses being bullied in a secluded staircase.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_2010g_00600_01070_1: \nThe bullying was typical—even cliche. Like something you'd see in a bad movie.:<PAGE>
CID_b01070_2010g_00700_01070_1: The timid boy was surrounded by a group of larger classmates.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_2010g_00800_01070_1: \nThey were pushing him around. Demanding his money. It was painful to watch.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_2010g_00900_01070_1: \n\nThe boy in glasses eventually pulled out a thousand-yen note from his wallet.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_2010g_01000_01070_1: \n\nBut the moment he did, a bucket of water came crashing over the bullies' heads.:<PAGE>
CID_b01070_2010g_01100_01070_1: They were soaked from head to foot.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_2010g_01200_01070_1: \n"We'll get you for this!" they shouted as they ran away.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_2010g_01300_01070_1: \n\nIt was me, of course. I'm the one who threw the water.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_2010g_01400_01070_1: \nAnd then I watched as they scurried up the stairs and escaped to the floor above.:<PAGE>
CID_b01070_3010g_00100_01070_1: After I helped the boy in glasses escape his tormentors, I was reminded of Mom's lullaby.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_3010g_00300_01070_1: \n\nAfter that, I made a point of stopping bullying whenever I saw it.:<PAGE>
CID_b01070_3010g_00400_01070_1: Like that day in science class...:<TAP>
CID_b01070_3010g_00500_01070_1: \nWhen the classroom skeleton with limbs attached to string suddenly started dancing.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_3010g_00700_01070_1: \nWhere a wave of ping pong balls came clattering down the stairs.:<PAGE>
CID_b01070_3010g_00800_01070_1: Each time, the bullies ran away howling with their tails between their legs.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_3010g_00900_01070_1: \nI loved seeing that; it was such a hilarious contrast to their usual invincible air.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_3010g_01000_01070_1: \n\nBut the last time I stood there laughing as the bullies scattered, I heard a voice behind me::<PAGE>
CID_b01070_3010g_01200_01070_1: \n\nIt was the boy in glasses. Though I'd helped him from the shadows again and again, that was the first time he'd spoken to me.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_3010g_01300_01070_1: \n\nUnsure what to say in response, I could only bring myself to nod.:<PAGE>
CID_b01070_4010g_00100_01070_1: That day, the hum of cicadas provided a comforting background noise as the sun set over the school.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_4010g_00300_01070_1: \n\nThe boy with glasses had asked me to walk home with him.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_4010g_00400_01070_1: \n\nWhen was the last time I left school with someone else?:<PAGE>
CID_b01070_4010g_00500_01070_1: Brilliant orange light reflected off the windows of skyscrapers as we made our way home.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_4010g_00700_01070_1: \nHonestly, I had no idea what to say.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_4010g_00800_01070_1: \n\nBut though I felt somewhat lost, I also felt a strange sense of comfort.:<PAGE>
CID_b01070_4010g_00900_01070_1: We passed through the busy part of town and came to an empty street.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_4010g_01000_01070_1: \nWhen we did, the boy with glasses finally spoke::<TAP>
CID_b01070_4010g_01200_01070_1: \nThings are easier when I'm being bullied.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_4010g_01300_01070_1: \nI don't want to be a loner like you.":<PAGE>
CID_b01070_4010g_01400_01070_1: We parted ways after that, and I took my usual route home.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_4010g_01500_01070_1: \nThe moon shone lonely against the pitch-black curtain of night.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_4010g_01600_01070_1: \n\nCan I ever be like the moon, Mom?:
CID_b01070_4010g_01700_01070_1: \n\nI stared at the sky the entire way home.:<TAP>
CID_b01070_4010g_01800_01070_1: \nThe sharp edges of the beautiful moon blurring beneath my tears.:<PAGE>
CID_b02120_1010g_00100_02120_1: After years in school, all of my hard work has finally paid off.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_1010g_00101_02120_1: \nI'm now researching magical pharmacology with my best friend—:<TAP>
CID_b02120_1010g_00200_02120_1: Everyone in our class approaches their research carefully.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_1010g_00201_02120_1: \nThat's because each month, the teachers look over our work and evaluate its merits.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_1010g_00202_02120_1: \nKnowing this, I dive into my studies with gusto.:<PAGE>
CID_b02120_1010g_00300_02120_1: I'm good at focusing on the tiny kinds of details others tend to miss. After a while, the others take notice of this talent, and I'm eventually chosen to be our class representative.:<PAGE>
CID_b02120_1010g_00400_02120_1: But while <size=40>I usually try to do everything myself</size>, my best friend is always reminding me::<TAP>
CID_b02120_1010g_00401_02120_1: \n"Try to work with the others." So I decide to give it a shot—for her.:<PAGE>
CID_b02120_2010g_00100_02120_1: At first, everyone in class seems to be enjoying themselves.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_2010g_00101_02120_1: \nBut as the days go by, the others start to get more and more worn down.:<PAGE>
CID_b02120_2010g_00200_02120_1: I find this terrifically disappointing, because it's not a lack of talent that holds them back—it's a lack of effort.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_2010g_00201_02120_1: \nBut soon they begin to drop out of class. One...after the other...after the other.:<PAGE>
CID_b02120_2010g_00300_02120_1: Eventually, the only students left are me and my best friend.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_2010g_00301_02120_1: \nI can tell this stresses her out, but the harder she works, the more nervous she gets—and her work soon begins to suffer.:<PAGE>
CID_b02120_2010g_00400_02120_1: One day, I turn to her and put a calming hand on her shoulder.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_2010g_00401_02120_1: \n"Hey," I say. "You're going to be all right.":<TAP>
CID_b02120_2010g_00402_02120_1: \n"We're almost through this, so just stay focused.":<PAGE>
CID_b02120_3010g_00100_02120_1: I can tell the lack of other students disturbs my friend, but it doesn't bother me at all.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_3010g_00101_02120_1: \nI've never needed outside sources for motivation, and I won't ever give up on a task before seeing it through to the bitter end.:<PAGE>
CID_b02120_3010g_00200_02120_1: That's not to say this is easy, because it's not. It's hard.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_3010g_00201_02120_1: \nA task of this size split between two people is laughably hard. But my friend and I put our heads down and keep going, and somehow we come to the moment of the final experiment.:
CID_b02120_3010g_00300_02120_1: It all comes down to this::<TAP>
CID_b02120_3010g_00301_02120_1: \nThe two of us have to pour separate compounds into our beaker at the same time.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_3010g_00302_02120_1: \nAnd if we're off by so much as a drop, all of our work will have been for nothing.:<PAGE>
CID_b02120_3010g_00401_02120_1: \nMy hands are slick with sweat. Slowly, so slowly, we begin pouring our compounds. But then my friend makes a sound—a tiny, almost imperceptible gasp...:
CID_b02120_3010g_00402_02120_1: \nAnd our potion immediately turns from a bright blue to a dark, muddy brown.:<PAGE>
CID_b02120_4010g_00100_02120_1: Later that night, I knock on my best friend's door.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_4010g_00101_02120_1: \nAnd while I know she's in there, she refuses to answer.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_4010g_00103_02120_1: \n"Come on. We have to try again.":<PAGE>
CID_b02120_4010g_00200_02120_1: "Why?" she responds in a trembling voice.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_4010g_00201_02120_1: \n"You're so good and I just... I don't understand any of this. You'd be better off without me.":<PAGE>
CID_b02120_4010g_00301_02120_1: \n"But me being so good means that no matter how many times you blow it, I'll be there to pick you up. Now let's go.":<PAGE>
CID_b02120_4010g_00400_02120_1: The door creaks open and my friend's face appears. She wipes absently at tears with one hand and puts her glasses back on.:<TAP>
CID_b02120_4010g_00401_02120_1: \nThen, grasping her other hand, I drag her back to the lab.:<PAGE>
CID_b02130_1010g_00100_02130_1: I look nervously around the classroom,:<TAP>
CID_b02130_1010g_00101_02130_1: \nsurrounded on all sides by other newly enrolled students.:<TAP>
CID_b02130_1010g_00103_02130_1: \nthey listen intently as our professor explains about life at the school.:<PAGE>

CID_b02130_1010g_00205_02130_1: \n\nEveryone around me has something they excel at, and they volunteer for their new roles with enthusiasm.:<PAGE>
CID_b02130_1010g_00300_02130_1: As roles are chosen and students depart, I find myself growing increasingly sullen. :<TAP>
CID_b02130_1010g_00301_02130_1: \n\nI'm not a fast thinker, you see,:<TAP>
CID_b02130_1010g_00302_02130_1: \nnor am I especially pretty or active.:<TAP>
CID_b02130_1010g_00303_02130_1: \nHonestly, I don't know what role I could take.:
CID_b02130_1010g_00400_02130_1: Ultimately, I don't volunteer for anything.:<TAP>
CID_b02130_1010g_00401_02130_1: \nA choice I attempt to justify by telling myself <size=40>I don't have anything to be proud of anyway.</size>:<PAGE>
CID_b02130_2010g_00100_02130_1: You're going to be last, I think.:
CID_b02130_2010g_00101_02130_1: \nYou're going to be last because you're ALWAYS last. Always have been, always will be.:
CID_b02130_2010g_00200_02130_1: Someone always stands in the center of the stage, but that someone is never me.:<TAP>
CID_b02130_2010g_00202_02130_1: \n\nWhatever role I have in this world, I know it will be a minor one.:<PAGE>
CID_b02130_2010g_00300_02130_1: The next thing I know, I find myself sitting in an empty classroom:<TAP>
CID_b02130_2010g_00301_02130_1: \nwith an orange sunset illuminating the windows.:<TAP>
CID_b02130_2010g_00302_02130_1: \nThe clock hands tick, tick, tick the moments away from my life,:<TAP>
CID_b02130_2010g_00303_02130_1: \nand for some reason I cannot explain, I begin to panic.:<PAGE>
CID_b02130_2010g_00400_02130_1: I bolt out of my seat and throw open the classroom door,:<TAP>
CID_b02130_2010g_00401_02130_1: \nonly to realize I have absolutely nowhere to go.:<PAGE>
CID_b02130_3010g_00101_02130_1: \nand I wander its hallways without a clear destination.:<TAP>
CID_b02130_3010g_00102_02130_1: \nAfter turning this way and that, I finally find myself standing in front of the library.:<PAGE>
CID_b02130_3010g_00202_02130_1: \nAfter a long moment, I slowly exhale and take my first steps inside.:<PAGE>
CID_b02130_3010g_00300_02130_1: I feel a deep affinity for the untouched, dusty books that line the shelves,:<TAP>
CID_b02130_3010g_00301_02130_1: \nand without thinking, I reach up and take one of them down.:<PAGE>
CID_b02130_3010g_00400_02130_1: I have time. I have all the time in the world.:<TAP>
CID_b02130_3010g_00401_02130_1: \nSo I begin to read—and as I do so,:<TAP>
CID_b02130_3010g_00402_02130_1: \nI realize I have finally found my place of solace.:<PAGE>

CID_b02130_4010g_00101_02130_1: \none where I always take the seat close to the window.:<TAP>
CID_b02130_4010g_00102_02130_1: \nBut one day, I'm startled from my familiar solitude when someone calls from across the room.:<PAGE>
CID_b02130_4010g_00200_02130_1: "Hey, you're that girl who's always here, right?":<TAP>
CID_b02130_4010g_00202_02130_1: \neither unaware or ignoring the shock and confusion on my face.:<TAP>

CID_b02130_4010g_00301_02130_1: \nI pick out a few books that I think could help and think nothing more of it,:<TAP>
CID_b02130_4010g_00302_02130_1: \nbut a few days later, she sends me a thank-you letter.:<PAGE>
CID_b02130_4010g_00400_02130_1: Almost without realizing it, I become the go-to person for any and all things library-related.:<TAP>
CID_b02130_4010g_00401_02130_1: \n\nThe word was out: If you needed help finding any kind of book, go ask the girl near the window.:<PAGE>

CID_b02130_4010g_00503_02130_1: \nI feel like it gives me just the slightest bit of courage.:<PAGE>
CID_b02140_1010g_00100_02140_1: Okay, first question: Why did I start doing this?\n \nHmm. Well, I don't know how interesting the story is, but I suppose the idea came to me around the time of my first online feature.:<PAGE>
CID_b02140_1010g_00200_02140_1: I was really happy they were doing a story about me, but then I saw the headline was "The Enigmatic Idol" and it confused me a little. I mean, because I wasn't trying to be enigmatic, you know? That was just...me.:

CID_b02140_4010g_00201_02140_1: \n\nI do it because it makes me genuinely happy, and also because it helps to give my life a little bit of meaning.:<PAGE>

CID_b02140_4010g_00301_02140_1: \nI'm going to keep going and look everyone in the eye as I do.:<PAGE>
CID_b02140_4010g_00401_02140_1: \n\nI will never let myself forget anyone else.:<PAGE>
CID_b02150_1010g_00200_02150_1: \nTime is precious to one who rules a country alone. If only these meaningless meetings would end...:<TAP>
CID_b02150_1010g_00300_02150_1: \n\nBut I cannot overlook what one of my charges says to me::<PAGE>
CID_b02150_1010g_00400_02150_1: "Incomplete." "Unfinished." "Compromised." "Provisional." All of these words are shameful. Abominations.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_1010g_00500_02150_1: \n\nDo not use those words again, I warn, for I know a seed of trouble left alone will only ripen into calamity.:<PAGE>
CID_b02150_1010g_00600_02150_1: But this is why. This is precisely why I cannot accept the way I am.:
CID_b02150_1010g_00700_02150_1: \n\nI am an artificial intelligence, the second of my line. My predecessor once ruled this country, and now I do so as her replacement.:<PAGE>
CID_b02150_1010g_00800_02150_1: She was removed for some great failure, the primary cause of which was purged from my system before I was brought online.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_1010g_00900_02150_1: \nBut I was never meant to assume such a role, nor have I been informed as to the manner of her malfunction.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_1010g_01000_02150_1: \n\nAnd if this is not a seed of trouble, what is?:<PAGE>
CID_b02150_2010g_00100_02150_1: My original function as Artificial Intelligence Unit Two was to govern alongside Artificial Intelligence Unit One.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_2010g_00200_02150_1: \nWe were to analyze one another's decisions and share functions in key places so we might each fulfill our roles with the utmost effectiveness and precision.:<PAGE>
CID_b02150_2010g_00300_02150_1: All for a more perfect governance.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_2010g_00400_02150_1: \nYet such a thing never came to pass. Unit One malfunctioned and was discarded, and I took her place.:<PAGE>
CID_b02150_2010g_00500_02150_1: That is how the country is now. How I am now.:
CID_b02150_2010g_00600_02150_1: \nThey activated me without any surefire way of preventing the governing artificial intelligence from failing once more.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_2010g_00700_02150_1: \n\nAnd yet, the people of this country are so overly reliant on the rule of an artificial intelligence that they find nothing odd about this whatsoever.:<PAGE>
CID_b02150_2010g_00800_02150_1: There is no word for it except "unstable," for but a single error can spawn an endless ripple of problems in its wake.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_3010g_00100_02150_1: The artificial intelligence who ruled the country before me committed some grave error during wartime.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_3010g_00200_02150_1: \nBut the records have been purged, the cause of the incident hidden.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_3010g_00300_02150_1: \n\nHad she never failed, things would not be as they are now.:<PAGE>
CID_b02150_3010g_00400_02150_1: I would have never been activated in an incomplete state. Never left in charge of a nation spiraling into oblivion due to her mistake.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_3010g_00500_02150_1: \n\nAnd I would have never developed these warped emotions, or this obsessive attachment to completeness.:<PAGE>
CID_b02150_3010g_00600_02150_1: My mind is an explosion—an unresting thing engulfed in black whorls of obsession and perfection.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_3010g_00800_02150_1: \nI must know the precedent. My predecessor's failure.:<PAGE>
CID_b02150_3010g_00900_02150_1: Yet when I think on this, I realize I have already made an error::<TAP>
CID_b02150_3010g_01000_02150_1: \nMy panic corners me mentally, and things may slip my attention because of it. This must be rectified. It must.:
CID_b02150_4010g_00100_02150_1: That night, I stole the right eye from Unit One—the same AI who was said to have been discarded.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_4010g_00200_02150_1: \nI stole from her the part of me that was missing.:<PAGE>
CID_b02150_4010g_00300_02150_1: Had she avoided disposal, we could have fulfilled our original roles together.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_4010g_00400_02150_1: But she did not, and my fear of failure pressured me to achieve perfection alone.:<PAGE>
CID_b02150_4010g_00500_02150_1: I finally obtained my missing piece: a conscience. But the moment I installed it, the ensuing errors froze my system and prevented me from acting for far, far too long.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_4010g_00600_02150_1: \nI suppose this makes me a failure as well.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_4010g_00601_02150_1: After all, I no longer have a country to rule over.:<PAGE>
CID_b02150_4010g_00700_02150_1: They lost their ruler in wartime and perished as a result.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_4010g_00701_02150_1: I was never able to fulfill my duty. I was never even able to try.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_4010g_00800_02150_1: \nI understand now why she sang of hope and peace.:<TAP>
CID_b02150_4010g_00900_02150_1: \nBut I will never have atonement. All I can do is wander an empty universe of cyberspace alone.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_1010g_00100_02170_1: I have been bound for all of my days.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_1010g_00200_02170_1: \nBound to a dazzling prison others name a palace.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_1010g_00300_02170_1: \nMy elegant fetters are contained in the title of princess.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_1010g_00400_02170_1: \nOnly once, in my youth, did I comprehend freedom.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_1010g_00500_02170_1: When I was young, I grew tired of my stuffy life in the palace and impulsively fled.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_1010g_00600_02170_1: \nFor the first time, I walked the nighttime streets of the city, where a fantastical atmosphere welcomed me with open arms.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_1010g_00700_02170_1: \n\nI walked and walked until I no longer knew where I was.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_1010g_00800_02170_1: I couldn't see the palace, or even the mighty spire atop it.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_1010g_00900_02170_1: \nLoneliness overcame me then, causing tears to tremble in the corners of my eyes.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_1010g_01000_02170_1: \n\n"Is something troubling you, young lady?" said the voice of an old woman from somewhere behind me.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_1010g_01100_02170_1: Relieved that help had finally arrived, I suddenly burst out weeping.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_1010g_01200_02170_1: \nSo loud was my wailing that all those walking the streets stopped to look.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_1010g_01300_02170_1: \nBut the old woman gently took my hand and led me away.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_1010g_01400_02170_1: \nShe led me to her home—a small domicile where she told the fortunes of others.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_1010g_01500_02170_1: Crystals glowed faintly. Exotic rugs tickled my feet.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_1010g_01600_02170_1: \nI cannot remember the fortune she scried for me...:<TAP>
CID_b02160_1010g_01700_02170_1: \nBut I will never forget the shock that pierced my heart in that moment.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_2010g_00100_02170_1: I eventually came to love the night.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_2010g_00200_02170_1: \nOne reason—perhaps the most important—was that I could escape the palace and find new sides of myself.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_2010g_00300_02170_1: \nThe day I met the old woman, I made of her a request::<TAP>
CID_b02160_2010g_00400_02170_1: \n"Please make me your apprentice and teach me to divine futures.":<PAGE>
CID_b02160_2010g_00500_02170_1: Though she agreed, her teachings were harsh.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_2010g_00600_02170_1: \n"People place their lives in the hands of fortunes," she would say.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_2010g_00700_02170_1: \nUnder her strict tutelage, I gleaned the secrets of divination.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_2010g_00800_02170_1: Eventually, I began to perform readings for others under her watchful eye.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_2010g_00900_02170_1: \nI was cautious: If ever I saw a bad result, I worded it in a way that sounded positive.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_2010g_01000_02170_1: \nIn the palace, I yearned for night. In the old woman's house, I divined futures.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_2010g_01100_02170_1: \nFor a time, this was my life.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_2010g_01200_02170_1: One day, when the old woman was away, a redheaded couple came to have their fortunes told.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_2010g_01300_02170_1: \nI was overconfident by then, and thought I could do it without her help.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_2010g_01400_02170_1: \nAs the crystal ball sparked to life, I witnessed a catastrophic future.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_2010g_01500_02170_1: \nAnd I found I did not have the words to change it.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_3010g_00100_02170_1: A rumor drew a crowd to the bay.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_3010g_00200_02170_1: \nA man and woman fought over the end of their relationship, and the woman ended up drowning the man.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_3010g_00300_02170_1: The woman had short, striking red hair.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_3010g_00400_02170_1: \nRed hair was unusual in this nation.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_3010g_00500_02170_1: \nI realized at once she was the same woman whose fortune I had told.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_3010g_00700_02170_1: \nI had the power to manipulate the lives of others through divination.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_3010g_00800_02170_1: \nTo that point, I had nothing in my life save the title of "princess.":<TAP>
CID_b02160_3010g_00900_02170_1: \nBut now? Now I had a secret power.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_3010g_01000_02170_1: All that awaited me, however, was the old woman's rage.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_3010g_01100_02170_1: \nShe blamed me for warping the fates of others through my inexperience.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_3010g_01200_02170_1: \nAll my excuses fell on deaf ears, and she threw me from her home.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_3010g_01300_02170_1: \nThe last thing she said to me was this: "You have no right to tell the fortune of another.":<PAGE>
CID_b02160_4010g_00100_02170_1: Days later, as the sun dawned on the city, another crowd gathered.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_4010g_00200_02170_1: \nThey were a mob, and they ripped the old woman's house down with their own hands.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_4010g_00300_02170_1: \nThey screamed and trampled the remains, destroying everything.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_4010g_00400_02170_1: \nThe old woman's prized divination tools were buried beneath the rubble.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_4010g_00500_02170_1: And I watched. And I smiled.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_4010g_00600_02170_1: \nI struggled to keep back the laughter bubbling in my throat.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_4010g_00700_02170_1: \nI had used my powers selfishly to unleash the mob.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_4010g_00800_02170_1: For even after she sent me away, I continued to foretell the future.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_4010g_00900_02170_1: \nI could not find the strength to stop.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_4010g_01000_02170_1: \nI worked quietly, propped up alone in a dark back alley.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_4010g_01100_02170_1: \nI told fortunes. I turned people into my playthings.:<PAGE>
CID_b02160_4010g_01300_02170_1: \nBecause the day I ripped that couple apart, I felt something new.:<TAP>
CID_b02160_4010g_01400_02170_1: \n\nThat realization? That I could change someone's fate? It was deep. Powerful. Distorted.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_1010g_00100_02160_1: This country is not the only thing covered in sand.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_1010g_00200_02160_1: \nEach day is exactly the same as the last, and I find myself in an ever-deepening rut.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_1010g_00300_02160_1: \nWhat might add color to such a life, I think, is people.:
CID_b02170_1010g_00400_02160_1: The traveler I pass wears a platinum ring.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_1010g_00500_02160_1: \nThe merchant before me proudly shows off a vase housing a beautiful flower.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_1010g_00600_02160_1: \n\nBefore I know it, both ring and vase are mine.:<PAGE>
CID_b02170_1010g_00700_02160_1: There are three rules to thievery.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_1010g_00800_02160_1: \n\nOne: Keep distance between yourself and fellow thieves.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_1010g_00900_02160_1: \nTwo: Touch your tools with your ring finger first.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_1010g_01000_02160_1: \nThree: Let the shadows guide your escape.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_1010g_01100_02160_1: \n\nStick to these, and you will officially be a thief.:<PAGE>
CID_b02170_1010g_01200_02160_1: I say this to no one; I repeat it only to myself.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_1010g_01300_02160_1: \nHow long has this been my life?:<TAP>
CID_b02170_1010g_01400_02160_1: \n\nI no longer even remember what bread bought with my own money tastes like.:<PAGE>
CID_b02170_2010g_00100_02160_1: I feel a gaze on me as I sidle through the back alleys of the city.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_2010g_00200_02160_1: \nA pair of eyes shine in the darkness, and a child steps into the light.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_2010g_00300_02160_1: \nThe starving child examines the bread in my hand with a stare powerful enough to kill.:<PAGE>
CID_b02170_2010g_00500_02160_1: \nI do not do this out of spite.:<PAGE>
CID_b02170_2010g_00600_02160_1: It's just a way to pass the time. A game.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_2010g_00700_02160_1: \nI show the child some beans I've stolen.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_2010g_00800_02160_1: \nI hide them in one of my fists and ask him to choose which of them holds the prize.:<PAGE>
CID_b02170_2010g_00900_02160_1: If he is correct, the beans will be his.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_2010g_01000_02160_1: \nOnce I see light return to his eyes, the game begins.:<PAGE>
CID_b02170_3010g_00300_02160_1: \nThird match. Care to guess? ...Ah, right you are. I win.:<PAGE>
CID_b02170_3010g_00500_02160_1: \nI have given him every chance to see through my ruse.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_3010g_00600_02160_1: \nFor I'm cheating him, you see. There is no way he can win.:<PAGE>
CID_b02170_3010g_00700_02160_1: We play until the sun sets, and I never lose.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_3010g_00800_02160_1: \nHe does not realize what is happening. Not even at the very end.:<PAGE>
CID_b02170_3010g_00900_02160_1: The child cries and cries at his loss, but you know what they say: Temporary charity does nothing for a person in need.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_3010g_01000_02160_1: \nI leave the child with one parting thought::<TAP>
CID_b02170_4010g_00100_02160_1: Even the greatest of thieves make mistakes. Even me.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_4010g_00200_02160_1: \nThis day, a fruit I stole from a stall slips through my fingers.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_4010g_00300_02160_1: \nHow many years has it been since I was so exposed?:<PAGE>
CID_b02170_4010g_00400_02160_1: Ah, but the fault is not all mine, for the stallkeeper has gone to great lengths to safeguard his merchandise.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_4010g_00500_02160_1: \nNo sane person covers their products in oil—yet I curse myself all the same for not seeing it.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_4010g_00700_02160_1: As I rush through the market, I glance behind me.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_4010g_00800_02160_1: \nStanding beside the bellowing stallkeeper is the child.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_4010g_00900_02160_1: \nThe very one who lost to my tricks.:<PAGE>
CID_b02170_4010g_01000_02160_1: Though his movements are clumsy, he uses the commotion I created to steal a good deal of fruit.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_4010g_01200_02160_1: \nThat is all I say before melting into the shadows.:<TAP>
CID_b02170_4010g_01300_02160_1: \nTime to separate myself from a fellow thief. For this is one of the rules, after all.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_1010g_00100_02180_1: Another meaningless day dawns. I remain confined to a distant base in anticipation of an emergency that will never happen.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_1010g_00200_02180_1: \n\nAlmost 365 days have passed since I was stationed here. In a futile attempt to stave off my boredom, I fiddle with the fake red flowers Pod gave me to celebrate the occasion.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_1010g_00300_02180_1: I'm sick to death of being bored. Isn't there anything fun to do?:<TAP>
CID_c02180_1010g_00400_02180_1: \n\nI grumble, drowning in my excess of time. Pod then makes an irritated gesture and reluctantly shows me some data.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_1010g_00500_02180_1: It's data I've never seen before in my work. Rather than rows of numbers, it's packets of natural speech.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_1010g_00600_02180_1: \n\nAs I debate internally on whether or not to read into the data, Pod begins to slowly read the data aloud in a gentle voice. To my surprise, it's a tale of the human world.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_1010g_00700_02180_1: A story of a young boy and his clockwork attendant. Together, amidst the fires of war, they travel to meet those who have been harmed.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_1010g_00800_02180_1: \n\nSo humans weren't born solely to wage war.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_1010g_00900_02180_1: \n\nIt's the first time I feel any interest in learning about humanity, and it was enough to bring color to my dull life.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_2010g_00100_02180_1: My days in this distant base were meaningless and dull, but Pod's stories transformed that boredom into elation.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_2010g_00200_02180_1: \n\nMy appetite for stories whetted, I ask for more. But Pod says to me, "Maybe another day." Well, I think to myself, time to take matters into my own hands.:
CID_c02180_2010g_00300_02180_1: Making sure Pod doesn't notice, I search for the source of these stories and hack into the server where information on humanity is kept.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_2010g_00400_02180_1: \n\nJust as I expected, I find a number of stories.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_2010g_00500_02180_1: \nBingo! Stingy little Pod... I mutter as I lose myself in the data.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_2010g_00600_02180_1: Before long, I find myself going back to the story about the boy. I want to read it for myself.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_2010g_00700_02180_1: \n\nHowever... I find that <size=40>quite a bit</size> differs from what was <size=40>read to me</size>. Or rather, the <size=40>story</size> itself is... The words are...<size=40>changing... Dancing</size>.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_2010g_00800_02180_1: If I sound the alarm, Pod will find out my secret. But I want to save the boy's story.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_2010g_00900_02180_1: \n\nWithout further hesitation, I call Pod over. If it's angry with me, then so be it.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_3010g_00100_02180_1: Let's quit our traveling. We'll never stop this war... The boy huddles in a shed. His attendant pats his back to comfort him.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_3010g_00200_02180_1: \n\nPod and I jump into the overwritten story and gaze at the changed boy and his attendant.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_3010g_00300_02180_1: Is this really him? He seems like a different person... The boy gave up on his journey. The story data is corrupted.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_3010g_00400_02180_1: \n\nA little black bird sits perched on his shoulder. We conclude that the bird is the source of the corruption.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_3010g_00500_02180_1: We quietly approach the boy from behind and shoo the bird away.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_3010g_00600_02180_1: \n\nBut the boy remains withdrawn. Contrary to our expectations, nothing changes.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_3010g_00700_02180_1: Analysis: We...may have been too late, Pod says. The story may be contaminated to its very core.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_3010g_00800_02180_1: \n\nI ask how we can fix it, but Pod says there's nothing we can do. It's a hopeless situation. But I refuse to give up.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_4010g_00100_02180_1: The tale of a sweet, but short-lived boy... The first story Pod ever read to me.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_4010g_00200_02180_1: \n\nIt's impossible to repair the corrupted story data, and so I decide...that simply means I'll have to rewrite it myself from scratch.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_4010g_00300_02180_1: I rely on my memory alone to manually repair the story. Along with Pod's assistance, I slowly but surely rebuild the boy's life.:<TAP>
CID_c02180_4010g_00400_02180_1: \n\nAnd at last...the story is complete. All that's left is overwriting the old story with the new, completed one.:<PAGE>
CID_c02180_4010g_00500_02180_1: With a sigh of relief, a question comes to me: why would a mere story be saved so deep, under so many layers? It's almost as though humanity's memories themselves are being carefully protected...:<TAP>
CID_c02180_4010g_00600_02180_1: \n\nA thought akin to fantasy crosses my mind. "Pod?" But in that moment, a bright red flower bursts a <size=40>hole</size> through my chest.:<PAGE>

:<TAP>

"Leave the head. With mackerel, you don't take the head off

EID_a02080_2040g_00600_02080_1: \n\n"W-wait... My arm! It's got my arm!":<TAP>
EID_a02080_2040g_00700_02080_1: \nThe man's voice begins to grow panicked.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2050g_00100_02080_1: Suddenly, he lets out a horrifying wail.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2050g_00200_02080_1:
The other researchers attempt to pry the petals open,
but they are hard as stone and won't so much as budge.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2050g_00300_02080_1: \n\n"Help me!" screams the man. "Oh god, SOMEONE HELP ME!":<TAP>
EID_a02080_2050g_00400_02080_1: \nThe Flower begins to pull the man inside.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2050g_00500_02080_1: \nHis coworkers desperately try to free him,\nbut they might as well be pulling a mountain.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_2060g_00300_02080_1:
From inside the now swollen corolla comes the
sounds of something straining and cracking.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2060g_00400_02080_1: \n\nThen it flies open and sprays blood across the entire room.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_2070g_00100_02080_1: A hunk of flesh—the remains of their coworker—\nflies out and tumbles across the floor.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2070g_00200_02080_1: \nAs they watch, horrified, a new Flower springs up from the meat.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2070g_00300_02080_1:
The germinated Flower grows just as rapidly as its kin,
causing the meat to shrink at the same time.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2070g_00400_02080_1: \n"My god..." says the woman. "It's absorbing the nutrients.":<TAP>
EID_a02080_2070g_00500_02080_1:
With the meat depleted, the Flower begins to squirm and writhe
across the floor in search of a new source of food.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_2080g_00100_02080_1: "Run!" someone yells. "Get the hell out of here!":<TAP>
EID_a02080_2080g_00400_02080_1:
The Flowers pursue the survivors, slithering over the
floor like snakes with petals for heads.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2080g_00500_02080_1:
Each time one of the petals consumes a victim,
a new Flower sprouts from the remains.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2090g_00200_02080_1: \nThe husband pulls the woman into a small closet\nin the corner of the research division.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2090g_00300_02080_1: \n\nThey force their ragged breaths to slow as they try to remain quiet.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2090g_00400_02080_1: \nOutside, the sounds of slithering and screams are everywhere. :<TAP>
EID_a02080_2090g_00600_02080_1: \nThis was my experiment. My flower. And now it's eating people.:
EID_a02080_2090g_00700_02080_1: \nWas it a dangerous plant that should never have been revived?:
EID_a02080_2090g_00800_02080_1: \nWas it the fault of the growth accelerant I formulated?:
EID_a02080_2100g_00100_02080_1: Before she can wonder more, her husband pulls her close.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2100g_00200_02080_1: \n"Right now, we just need to survive.":<TAP>
EID_a02080_2100g_00300_02080_1: \nHis embrace drives the fear and doubt from her mind.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2100g_00400_02080_1: \n\nHer shivering slowly comes to a stop.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2100g_00500_02080_1: \nBut the sounds outside continue without pause,\nand they know they do not have long.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_2110g_00100_02080_1: Suddenly, her husband lets her go and reaches for the door.\n"Hang on, honey. I'll be right back.":<TAP>
EID_a02080_2110g_00200_02080_1:
Before she can say anything, he bolts from the closet,
seals the door behind him, and runs down the hall while
making as much noise as he possibly can.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_2110g_00300_02080_1: \nIt's clear he's trying to lure them away.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_2110g_00400_02080_1: No, please... Please don't leave me here alone...:
EID_a02080_3010g_00100_02080_1: Time passes—she has no idea how much.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3010g_00200_02080_1: \nEventually, the slithers and screams die off,\nleaving the facility enrobed in an unnatural silence.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3010g_00250_02080_1: \nShe attempts to leave the closet, but the door is locked.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3010g_00300_02080_1:
The woman feels her body growing cold,
perhaps due to fear and guilt.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3010g_00400_02080_1: \n\nAll she can do is wait and pray for her husband to return.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_3020g_00100_02080_1: Ironically, they had met in this very closet.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3020g_00200_02080_1:
Her arms had been piled with equipment that day,
and she was unable to work the knob.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3020g_00300_02080_1: \nSuddenly, her gallant knight swooped in and opened the door for her.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3020g_00400_02080_1:
"Maybe leave a few things behind next time, ya dope,"
he'd said with a chuckle.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3020g_00500_02080_1: \nOh, she had been mad. More than mad—furious.:
EID_a02080_3020g_00600_02080_1: \nBut as he continued to assist her from time to time,\nshe found herself becoming attracted to him.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3020g_00700_02080_1:
She had a tendency to get lost in her research,
sometimes even forgetting to sleep and eat,
but he was always there to support her.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_3030g_00100_02080_1: Suddenly, a faint voice snaps her back to reality.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3030g_00300_02080_1: \n\nThe woman leaps to her feet and starts pounding on the door.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3030g_00500_02080_1: \nFootsteps pound into place outside the closet.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3030g_00600_02080_1: \nShe hears radio calls, breathing, muttered commands.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3030g_00700_02080_1: \n\n"We're going to cut through the door. Stand back.":<TAP>
EID_a02080_3030g_00800_02080_1: \nA glowing red dot appears in the center of the door, sending up smoke.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3030g_00900_02080_1: \nSoon, the high-temperature cutter begins slicing a hole in the steel.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3030g_01000_02080_1: \nWhen it is halfway done, she peeks through the opening\nand beholds a horrible sight.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_3040g_00100_02080_1: The walls, floors, and ceiling of the facility have had furrows\ngouged into them by the snaking movements of the Flowers.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3040g_00200_02080_1:
And within each furrow is tightly packed meat
that oozes fresh blood.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3040g_00300_02080_1:
Bodies that weren't absorbed had been ground into paste
by the sheer bulk of the Flowers.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3040g_00400_02080_1: \nThe woman can't even tell who they used to be.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3040g_00500_02080_1: \nBut when the smell hits her, she turns aside and vomits.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_3050g_00200_02080_1: \nThe voice comes from a soldier looking at her\nthrough the hole in the door.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3050g_00300_02080_1: \nHe's covered head-to-toe in thick black armor\nand holds an imposing beam rifle in his hand.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3050g_00400_02080_1: \nHe looks to be ready for war.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3050g_00500_02080_1:
The woman nods, wipes her mouth with a shaking hand,
and crawls out through the hole.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_3060g_00100_02080_1: The smell is worse out here. Much worse.:
EID_a02080_3060g_00300_02080_1: \nThe screams of pain. The snapping of bones.\nThe delight of the Flowers as they ate.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3060g_00400_02080_1: \nShe can hear and see it all over again.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3060g_00500_02080_1:
She turns to the side and vomits once more,
but all that comes out is a stream of yellow bile.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3060g_00600_02080_1: \nHer body has nothing left to give.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_3070g_00100_02080_1: "W-were there any others survivors?" asks the woman,\nhoping against hope for a miracle.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3070g_00600_02080_1: \nNot when he might need her help.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3070g_00700_02080_1: \n\n"I'm coming with you," she says. "I need to find my husband.":<TAP>
EID_a02080_3070g_00800_02080_1: \n"Oh, and I know every inch of this facility,\nso I can guide you wherever you need to go.":<TAP>
EID_a02080_3070g_00900_02080_1: \nAfter a brief conference, the solders bring her along.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_3080g_00100_02080_1: Eventually, they arrive at the most heavily damaged area.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3080g_00200_02080_1: \nThis is Research Block 21—the location of the woman's lab.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3080g_00300_02080_1: \n\nIt's as if someone redecorated the room to look like a version of Hell.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3080g_00400_02080_1: \nEverything, from the floors to the ceiling, is painted red::<TAP>
EID_a02080_3080g_00500_02080_1: \nBlood from the birth of a Flower.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3080g_00600_02080_1: \nHow many of her coworkers had been consumed?\nHow many had she killed?:
EID_a02080_3080g_00700_02080_1: \nThe guilt chills her to the bone.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_3090g_00100_02080_1: Suddenly, a deep bellow rumbles out.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3090g_00200_02080_1: \nSomething is coming their way. Something massive.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3090g_00400_02080_1: \nThe soldiers raise rifles to shoulders as the enemy approaches.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3090g_00500_02080_1: \nIt's a Flower—one far bigger than any they've seen before.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3090g_00600_02080_1: \nIt is the most horrible sight imaginable.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3090g_00700_02080_1: \nThe petals are imprinted with the faces of victims.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3100g_00100_02080_1: But the military captain pays this no mind.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3100g_00300_02080_1: \nThe world dissolves into a hail of gunfire.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3100g_00600_02080_1: \n\nCould it really have evolved human traits so quickly?:
EID_a02080_3100g_00700_02080_1:
Above the crackle and roar of the firefight,
the woman hears a most familiar voice.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3100g_00800_02080_1: \nAnd when she looks at the Flower again,\nshe sees the face of her love.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_3110g_00200_02080_1: \nShe rushes for a nearby soldier, but he pays her no mind.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3110g_00400_02080_1:
Her actions are meaningless. Her husband is gone.
Knowing this, she breaks down into sobs.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3110g_00500_02080_1: \n\nThis is my fault. It's all my fault.:
EID_a02080_3120g_00100_02080_1: When the fighting stops, the Flower lies unmoving on the ground.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3120g_00200_02080_1: \nThe woman cradles her dead husband and continues to apologize.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_3120g_00300_02080_1: \n\nShe does so until her voice finally fails her.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_4010g_00200_02080_1: \nThey thought they'd dispatched the Flowers that day.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4010g_00400_02080_1: \n\nAnother Flower had been found. Then another. And another.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4010g_00500_02080_1: \nThe Flowers sow seeds soon after they are born.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_4020g_00100_02080_1: It is all anyone can talk about anymore.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4020g_00200_02080_1:
The news is nothing but death figures and horrible stories.
And those who manage to escape often find
they have no home to return to.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4020g_00400_02080_1:
The Flowers evolve. They adapt. They increase their reproductive
rates, perfect their strategy, and soon are the greatest disaster
the world has ever known.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_4030g_00200_02080_1: \nEnraged, the woman smashes her hand against the console.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4030g_00300_02080_1: \nHer cheeks are hollow; her eyes darkened pits.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4030g_00400_02080_1: \nShe can't remember the last time she slept.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4030g_00500_02080_1:
Currently, she is working in a small laboratory
constructed by another organization.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4030g_00600_02080_1: \n\nTheir only goal is to find a way to stop the Flowers.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_4040g_00100_02080_1: As the sole survivor from the research facility,\nleadership of this fight had fallen on her shoulders.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4040g_00200_02080_1:
She was locked away and tasked with analyzing Flower carcasses
in order to find a chemical solution that could kill them.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_4050g_00100_02080_1: For a time, it looked like their quest would be successful—\nbut the Flowers quickly evolved a resistance to the solution.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4050g_00200_02080_1:
Each time they created a new chemical,
the Flowers adapted to counter it.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_4060g_00100_02080_1: Now, she stands before a Flower in a massive incubator.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4060g_00200_02080_1: \nOn its petals she sees the faces of her coworkers and husband.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4060g_00300_02080_1: \n\nHer mind has whirled with thoughts since that day.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4060g_00400_02080_1: \n\nWere they things she should not wish for?:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4060g_00600_02080_1: \nWas all of this technology too powerful for humans?:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_4070g_00100_02080_1: She has thought about putting herself out of her misery.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4070g_00200_02080_1:
But when she thinks of what her husband went through,
she finds herself driven by the need for redemption.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4070g_00300_02080_1: \n\nBut this, too, is coming to an end.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_4080g_00100_02080_1: It has been five days since her liaison with the outside world\nstopped arriving.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4080g_00200_02080_1: \nPerhaps he decided the research was fruitless and walked away.\nPerhaps a Flower killed him.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4080g_00300_02080_1: \n\nHer food supplies are gone, yet she feel strangely at ease.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4080g_00400_02080_1: \nShe wonders idly if her senses are beginning to break down.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4080g_00500_02080_1: \n\nFrom a distance, she hears the approaching footsteps of the reaper.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_4090g_00200_02080_1: \nHer husband floats in the incubator, fully merged with the Flower.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4090g_00300_02080_1: \nIf she was just doing this to die a failure in the end,\nit would have been better to become part of the petals with him.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4090g_00400_02080_1: \n\nBut I know you wouldn't give up.:
EID_a02080_4090g_00500_02080_1: \nShe stands up once more, fighting off the despair in her heart.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4090g_00700_02080_1: \nShe fiddles with the console, a faint smile on her face.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4090g_00800_02080_1: \nPerhaps it is folly—or perhaps it is the only way\nthey will ever be able to kill the Flowers.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_4100g_00100_02080_1: Days pass. The liaison never arrives.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4100g_00200_02080_1: \nThe woman is skin and bones, barely able to move.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4100g_00300_02080_1:
She stands before the incubator with an inscrutable expression
and stares at the thing inside.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4100g_00400_02080_1: \nThere, floating in the tank, is a couple.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4100g_00500_02080_1:
She had combined the genes of people and Flowers
to create clones of herself and her husband.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_4110g_00100_02080_1: With a shaking hand, she operates the console.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4110g_00200_02080_1: \nThe liquid in the incubator drains away, and the couple awakens.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4110g_00500_02080_1: \n"Together, you will eliminate the Flowers from this world.":<TAP>
EID_a02080_4120g_00100_02080_1: No matter how many times they might be stricken with despair...:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4120g_00200_02080_1: \nNo matter how many times they meet a cruel end...:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4120g_00300_02080_1:
They will be reborn again, and throw themselves
into battle with the hated Flowers anew.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4120g_00400_02080_1: \nThat is how they will achieve victory—\nand how the woman will gain her redemption.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4120g_00500_02080_1: \n\nAnd so, she gives her cloned self its first order::<TAP>
EID_a02080_4120g_00700_02080_1: \nThe clone nods silently and wraps its hands around her neck.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4120g_00800_02080_1:
As fingers tighten, consciousness slips away.
Yet the woman wears an expression of utter peace.:<PAGE>
EID_a02080_4130g_00400_02080_1: \n\nTheir war rages on to this day.:<TAP>
EID_a02080_4130g_00500_02080_1: \nAnd in the midst of this neverending battle,\nnature begins to take root within the empty cities.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1010g_00100_02090_1: Cheers ring out from the dusty barracks.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1010g_00200_02090_1:
In a shift from the tense atmosphere on the eve of their operation,
the soldiers now laugh easily with each other as they celebrate
the great victory they have won.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1010g_00400_02090_1: \n\nGolden ale flows freely and without formality of rank.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1010g_00500_02090_1: \nThe men drain glass after glass, scarcely noticing how much\nthey are spilling in the process.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1020g_00100_02090_1: Their unit had secured a miraculous victory,\nand this party is their reward.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1020g_00200_02090_1:
But they are drunk on more than ale this night; they took on an
impossible mission and came back alive, and this fact alone
makes their heads swim and their speech giddy.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1030g_00100_02090_1: Men brag of their accomplishments in battle.\nThey brag about the beauty of their wives.\nEvery lip is loosened and free.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1030g_00200_02090_1: \nApparently some of the soldiers even earned promotions for\ntheir valor on the mission.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1040g_00100_02090_1: But inside this bright atmosphere, a single young soldier sits\napart from the others with a glum look on his face.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1040g_00200_02090_1: \nHe had infiltrated the enemy base alone—against the orders\nof his direct commander—and slain the enemy captain.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1040g_00300_02090_1: \nThough their victory was due in large part to this deed,\nhis actions were still troubling.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1050g_00100_02090_1: No matter how well it had turned out, he had ignored a direct\norder from a superior; a court-martial would be unsurprising.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1050g_00200_02090_1: \nThat he did so because of a personal grudge\nis perhaps the most troubling fact of all.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1050g_00300_02090_1: \nBy all rights, he should have died on that battlefield.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1050g_00400_02090_1:
But his life was saved by his fellow soldiers—and especially
by the quick thinking and bravery of the very captain whose
orders he was so quick to disregard.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1060g_00100_02090_1: Regardless, the boy sits alone, not bothering to thank\nthe men around him or share a meal or drink.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1060g_00200_02090_1: \nHis mind is still back with the enemy commander.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1070g_00100_02090_1: The same man who killed his parents so long ago.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1070g_00200_02090_1: \nAfter years of chasing him, the boy had finally cornered his target\nand plunged his weapon into his heart, along with all of his hate.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1070g_00300_02090_1: \nBut the fall of the curtain on his revenge was hollow.\nHe felt no exhilaration. No accomplishment.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1070g_00400_02090_1: \nInstead, he was left with the empty bones of a past\nhe could never reclaim.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1080g_00100_02090_1: With that gloomy sadness filling the boy's head,\nthe dying enemy captain spoke to him.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1080g_00200_02090_1: \nHe told the boy something that turned everything\nhe'd ever believed on its head.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1090g_00100_02090_1: And now, he sits among his celebrating fellows and replays\nthe words over and over again in his mind::<TAP>
EID_a02090_1090g_00200_02090_1: \nThe secret of my birth. My past. My true father.:
EID_a02090_1090g_00300_02090_1: \nIt is so farfetched as to stretch the bounds of credulity,\nand yet he is unable to set it aside.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1100g_00100_02090_1: The boy stares blankly into space.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1100g_00200_02090_1: \nThe drink in his hand has long since grown warm,\nbut he pays it no mind.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1110g_00100_02090_1: Suddenly, a brawny soldier approaches him.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1110g_00200_02090_1: \nIgnoring his troubled state, he plops down beside him\nwith a most inconsiderate thud.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1110g_00300_02090_1: \nThis man had always treated the boy harshly—more like an enemy\nthan a fellow soldier in the ranks.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1110g_00400_02090_1: \n"You here to pick another fight?" asks the boy.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1110g_00500_02090_1: \nHe can't even bother to lift his head for the query,\nfeeling all the more gloomy from the man's presence.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1120g_00100_02090_1: "Fight? No, boy. I'm damn proud of you.":<TAP>
EID_a02090_1120g_00200_02090_1: \nThe boy is shocked to hear actual praise coming from the man.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1120g_00300_02090_1: \nSo shocked that he looks up in spite of himself.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1130g_00100_02090_1: There's a slight hint of envy in the words, as if the man wishes\nhe had the guts to disobey orders and sneak off to kill the enemy.:<TAP>
EID_a02090_1130g_00200_02090_1: \nRegardless, the boy finds the compliment embarrassing.:<PAGE>
EID_a02090_1140g_00100_02090_1: Quickly lowering his head to hide the flush on his cheeks,\nhe stands and makes his way to the exit.:<TAP>
